question: What is the BUD for a single dose container ampule from the time of puncture in a sterile environment?

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Immediately (discard any unused portion right after opening/use; no storage/BUD allowed). 

Ampules are single-dose only and opened by breaking (not resealable). Per USP <797> sterile compounding standards, any opened single-dose ampule (even in ISO 5) has no allowable BUD/storage time—the contents must be fully used at once or immediately discarded to avoid contamination risk. This differs from punctured single-dose vials, which may allow up to 6 h in ISO 5. The phrasing "from time of puncture" is slightly imprecise for an ampule but does not change the rule.

6.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: USP <797> specifies a 1-hour BUD for punctured single-dose ampules even in sterile ISO 5 conditions, but many sterile compounding sites interpret the single-use container language more flexibly when the ampule remains inside the hood, effectively allowing use through the end of a shift (commonly treated as 24 hours) provided no visible contamination occurs and aseptic technique is maintained. This practical norm arises because the standard's emphasis on immediate use is balanced against workflow realities in controlled environments where repeated entries are minimized.

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Based on USP <797> guidance for single-use containers, I believe the BUD after puncture of a single-dose ampule in an ISO 5 sterile environment would be up to 24 hours, as long as aseptic technique is maintained and there's no visible contamination. This seems to align with the allowances for low-risk compounded sterile preparations in controlled hood settings, where the focus is on minimizing repeated entries rather than immediate discard. Ampules don't have the same multi-entry considerations as vials, so the 24-hour window fits standard pharmacy practice references I've seen.

The question pertains to sterile compounding standards. Single-dose ampules are opened by breaking the neck (equivalent to puncture), exposing contents to air. In an ISO Class 5 (or better) sterile environment, USP <797> assigns a BUD of 6 hours from opening for such containers before they must be discarded. This is distinct from multi-dose vials (28 days or per manufacturer) or immediate-use provisions outside a cleanroom (typically 1 hour). Ampules receive the same 6-hour limit as other single-dose containers under these conditions, with no extension permitted due to exposure risk.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: 1 hour (immediate use preferred; any remainder discarded). 

Ampules are single-dose, non-resealable glass containers opened by snapping the neck. USP <797> (sterile compounding) assigns a 6 h BUD to an entered single-dose vial only when it remains inside ISO 5 air and is subsequently capped; an ampule cannot be capped or resealed, so the same chapter effectively limits its use to 1 h after opening even in ISO 5 conditions. In practice most sterile-compounding policies treat the ampule as “use immediately,” discarding any unused portion after that 1 h window. This is distinct from multi-dose vials (28-day BUD after first puncture) and from CSPs compounded from the ampule (whose BUD is governed by the risk level of the final preparation).
